description: Naval VTOL attack fighter, construction number recorded by russianplanes.net as 797786x3010xx with the final digits unread. Carries no bort number. Listed as a current exhibit in the russianplanes.net museum register, read September 2026. A second Yak-38 that stood here wearing "60 white" (c/n 7977864060699) has left the collection.

First flying prototype, izdeliye 48-2, the aircraft shown at Farnborough in 1992. Transferred from the Yakovlev OKB museum in 2009. Displayed in its old scheme with bort 75 and mock-ups of R-73 and R-27R missiles on the underwing pylons (kpopov.ru, updated 2021; russianplanes.net museum register, read September 2026).
VR-3 Reys reconnaissance drone. Brought from Khodynka Field; was still unrestored when photographed in 2016.
Works number 500AT15, series number 1615. Ex-Khodynka Field. Wore "59 red" when photographed in August 2019 and "71 blue" in the current russianplanes.net record.

High-altitude MiG-19SV, works number 0615337. Moved half-dismantled from Khodynka Field to the museum in 2012 (kpopov.ru). Year given as the MiG-19SV production year cited by kpopov.ru for this sub-type, not from a nameplate - treat with caution. Wears bort number 11; recorded without a tail number because another airframe of this type in the database already carries it.
Interceptor, works number 0915321. Photographed at the museum as "52 red" in August 2019 and still carried in the russianplanes.net museum register, read September 2026.
Training version of the Mi-1, bort "07 white".
Interceptor, serial number 1819.
Export-standard Mi-25 airframe, works number 35324246003035. At Khodynka Field until 2012.

Works number 2615334, recorded by kpopov.ru as requiring confirmation because no data plate was found. Served with the 1st Guards Bomber Regiment at Lebyazhye, then 559 BAP at Morozovsk; handed to the museum in kit form and reassembled, an intermediate assembly stage being photographed in June 2018.
Full-scale reproduction of Yakovlev's first aircraft of 1927. Not an original airframe.
Works number 310024, bort "37 yellow". Displayed indoors.
Bort "3 yellow", displayed indoors.
Stroy-P system reconnaissance drone, works number 611-4, bort "10 blue".

Recovered wreck under long-term restoration; recorded by russianplanes.net as fragments rather than a complete airframe. Raised from Lake Krivoye near Safonovo, Murmansk Oblast, in 2012 together with the museum's Yak-1.

Raised from Lake Krivoye near Safonovo-1 (Severomorsk-2 airfield), Murmansk Oblast, on 10 June 2012, from the 20th IAP of the Northern Fleet air force. Restored to static condition and displayed in the Sokoly Rossii hall.
Single-seat trainer displayed indoors.
Works number 1165312.
Works number 0115307. Displayed in the Sokoly Rossii hall in the markings of Hero of the Soviet Union I.I. Kleshchev with 14 red stars.
Reconnaissance drone, bort "023 black".
Two-seat trainer conversion, works number 115001, bort "01 yellow".

Works number 1712. The aircraft presented as the machine paid for by Ferapont Golovaty; flown post-war to the Air Force museum at Monino and moved to the Yakovlev OKB museum in Moscow in 1958 before reaching this collection.
Bort "25 yellow".

Defence-suppression MiG-25BM, works number 02022047, bort "47 blue". A recent arrival - it is not in the 2021 kpopov.ru survey of the collection but is carried in the russianplanes.net museum register, read September 2026.
Two-seat conversion trainer, works number 22040578, bort "22 blue". Came from the Gromov Flight Research Institute at Zhukovsky; not in the 2021 kpopov.ru survey.
Izdeliye 41, works number 1515301, bort "15 white". Second Su-24 in the collection; not in the 2021 kpopov.ru survey.
Izdeliye 242, works number 3532424015931, bort "92 yellow".
Search and rescue amphibian, works number 3602801, bort "04 yellow".

Works number 2960518450, bort "62 blue". kpopov.ru describes the museum's MiG-29 as the fifth prototype; the russianplanes.net card gives a series construction number, so that claim is not carried over here.

Ex-Belgian Air Force 52-7175, withdrawn January 1972, later at Koksijde and Bierset, damaged during a mock attack display at Bierset in September 1993 before coming to Russia. Carries FU-29 with UR-D and 3R-V codes also recorded.
Recovered from a lake in the Soviet Arctic after a 2001 archive find identified the crash site; displayed in the Sokoly Rossii hall. Restored from a recovered wreck (kpopov.ru, 2021).

Werknummer 411768, recovered near Nikel in Murmansk Oblast - undercarriage legs, fuselage, wing, engine and tail parts. The pilot, Feldwebel Willi Schlammer, was posted missing. Composite restoration from recovered wreckage.
Second Messerschmitt in the Sokoly Rossii hall, serial number 14232 per kpopov.ru. Restored from recovered wreckage.

Works number 61912538152 per kpopov.ru, bort 51 when photographed in April 2016. Listed by kpopov.ru in 2021 but russianplanes.net holds no card for a MiG-27 at this museum, so its continued presence in 2025-26 is not confirmed.
Long-range cruise missile displayed in the aviation area.
